1 رَاقَ , (JK, S, K,) aor. يَرِيقُ, inf. n. رَيْقٌ, (JK, S,) said of the سَرَاب [or mirage], It was agitated, and moved to and fro, (JK, K,) or it shone, or glistened, (S,) above the ground; (JK, S, K;) and ↓ تريّق signifies the same. (S, O, K.) [And in the former sense, راق may be said of water; for the inf. n.] رَيْقٌ signifies also The going to and fro (Lth, JK, K) of water, (JK,) or of
shallow water and the like, (Lth, K,) upon the surface of the earth. (Lth, JK, K.) ―
-b2- Also, (Ks, JK, Msb, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (Ks, Msb,) said of water, (Ks, JK, Msb, K,) and of blood, (Msb,) It poured out, or forth. (Ks, Msb, K.) ―
-b3- هُوَ يَرِيقُ بِنَفْسِهِ, (JK, S, K,) inf. n. رُيُوقٌ (S, K) and رَيْقٌ, (TA,) (tropical:) He gives up his spirit; or gives away his life; syn. يَجُودُ بِهَا; (JK, S, K;) at death: (S, K:) mentioned by Ks. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
